headline.headline: ORIOLES EXPLODE FOR FOUR IN THE SEVENTH TO DOWN PHILLIES, 6-4
headline.deck: Baltimore bats erupt in pivotal frame to snap tight game wide open
headline.body:
BALTIMORE — The Philadelphia Phillies arrived at Camden Yards with a 2-0 lead through six innings and looked every bit a team destined to leave Maryland with a road win. Then the seventh inning happened. The Baltimore Orioles sent four runs across the plate in that decisive frame, turning a deficit into a 6-4 lead they would not surrender, sending 31,857 fans home satisfied on a Friday night in Baltimore.

The game had been a taut, low-scoring affair through six innings of play. Philadelphia scratched out two runs in the first to set the early tone, added another in the third and one more in the sixth to build what appeared to be a workable cushion. Baltimore managed two runs in the first but had gone quiet against the Phillies pitching staff until the seventh inning erupted. Pitcher Painter earned the win on the evening, benefiting directly from that four-run outburst. Phillies reliever Kerkering hit Pete Alonso with a pitch during the frame, one of the uglier moments in an inning that quickly unraveled for Philadelphia.

The Orioles held the Phillies scoreless over the final three innings to close out the 6-4 victory. Baltimore's ability to manufacture a game-changing inning against a Phillies club that entered the night with genuine playoff aspirations makes this result one of the more significant of the AL-NL interleague calendar. The loss stings for Philadelphia, which had controlled the tempo for the better part of two hours before the seventh inning wiped the advantage off the board entirely.

secondary.headline: DIAMONDBACKS RALLY FOR FOUR IN EIGHTH TO STUN GUARDIANS, 4-1
secondary.deck: Arizona's late-inning surge extends win streak to four straight games
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND — Arizona trailed Cleveland 1-0 through seven innings and appeared headed for a quiet, forgettable loss. The Diamondbacks had other ideas. Arizona unloaded four runs in the top of the eighth inning Friday at Progressive Field to complete a stunning turnaround, leaving town with a 4-1 victory that extended their winning streak to four games. The win lifted Arizona to 58-52 in the NL West standings.

Guardians starter Tyler Bibee had a rough eighth inning on multiple fronts, hitting both Gabriel Moreno and Ketel Marte with pitches during a frame that ultimately cost Cleveland the ballgame. Cleveland had grabbed the lone run of the game back in the first inning but could not add to that total over the next six innings. The Guardians, sitting at 56-55 and third in the AL Central, absorbed a loss that felt decisive and damaging given how competently they had pitched through the first seven frames.

secondary.headline: PENGUINS LOCK UP NOVAK ON THREE-YEAR EXTENSION AS PLAYOFF RUN CONTINUES
secondary.deck: Pittsburgh rewards dependable forward with long-term security amid second-round action
secondary.body:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Penguins made a statement about their organizational direction Friday, signing forward Tommy Novak to a three-year contract extension. The move secures one of the team's more reliable contributors as the Penguins remain active in the NHL's second-round playoff action this May. Pittsburgh elected not to wait until the offseason to get the deal done, a sign the front office views Novak as a core piece of the franchise's competitive window.

Novak has drawn praise for his reliability and two-way game throughout his tenure in Pittsburgh. The extension removes any uncertainty about his future at a moment when the Penguins are focused squarely on advancing deeper into the postseason. Locking up a dependable forward mid-playoff run sends a message to the locker room about long-term commitment even as the team battles through the second round.

secondary.headline: ROZIER BETTING CASE HEATS UP AS ATTORNEYS ARGUE OVER DAMNING TEXT MESSAGE
secondary.deck: Defense claims co-defendant's message clears veteran guard of wrongdoing
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — The legal proceedings surrounding NBA veteran Terry Rozier took a pointed turn Friday as attorneys sparred over the meaning of a text message sent by a co-defendant in the betting case that has shadowed the guard's career. Rozier's legal team argued in a court filing that the text in question actually demonstrates their client did not engage in the conduct alleged, pushing back forcefully against the prosecution's characterization of the evidence.

The case has drawn sustained attention across the league during an otherwise busy stretch of second-round playoff basketball. Rozier, who built a reputation as one of the more dynamic guards in the Eastern Conference over the past several seasons, now faces a legal cloud that has kept him out of the playoff spotlight entirely. How courts interpret the disputed text message could prove central to whether the case against him holds up or begins to unravel.

column.headline: THE SEVENTH INNING IS WHERE BASEBALL GAMES GO TO DIE — OR COME ALIVE
column.body:
Two games on Friday night offered the same brutal lesson for any team that thinks a two-run lead late in a baseball game is something approaching safe. Baltimore scored four times in the seventh against Philadelphia. Arizona scored four times in the eighth against Cleveland. In both cases, the winning team had looked completely stuck at the plate for the better part of two hours before the dam broke all at once. That is the cruelest and most beautiful mathematics of this sport.

The Phillies and the Guardians will spend this Saturday morning replaying the same mental footage, wondering where exactly the game slipped away. The honest answer, in both cases, is that it slipped away in a single inning. One bad frame is all it takes. The Orioles and the Diamondbacks did not win those games because they were better teams for eight innings. They won them because baseball hands you twenty-seven outs and the last few can swallow everything that came before them whole.

story.headline: YANKS SILENCE WRIGLEY AS ROSARIO, JONES GO DEEP IN 2-0 BLANKING OF CUBS
story.deck: New York's back-to-back solo shots in the fourth proved all the pitching staff needed.
story.body:
CHICAGO, July 31 — Eddie Rosario and Jones combined to provide the only offense New York would need Friday night at Wrigley Field, each depositing a solo home run in the fourth inning as the Yankees shut out the Cubs 2-0 before 40,129 fans. The two solo shots — Rosario's 10th of the year and Jones's fourth — came in a game that was otherwise a pitching clinic, with neither team threatening seriously until the Yankees broke the deadlock in the fourth.

New York's pitching held Chicago scoreless across all nine innings, leaving the Cubs with six men stranded on base. The Yankees were hardly a freight train themselves, going quiet after their fourth-inning burst and stranding nine baserunners of their own. Miguel Amaya doubled for Chicago's most notable offensive moment, but the Cubs could not push anything across the plate in a game completed in a crisp 2 hours and 27 minutes.

Elsewhere around the National League, the Cincinnati Reds survived a wild 8-7 slugfest against Pittsburgh in which the Pirates sent three men across in the eighth inning to pull within one before the Reds held on. In Atlanta, a four-run sixth inning powered the Braves past Washington 6-2, with Olson blasting his 29th home run of the season. Abrams added his 28th as the Braves continued to build separation in the NL East.

story.headline: WEMBANYAMA SIGNS LONG-TERM NIKE DEAL, WILL RECEIVE SIGNATURE SHOE
story.deck: Spurs superstar joins elite company as Nike invests in generational French talent
story.body:
Victor Wembanyama, the 7-foot-3 Spurs phenom who has already reshaped how the basketball world thinks about size and skill, is getting his own sneaker. Sources told ESPN that Wembanyama signed a new, long-term deal with Nike that includes a signature shoe line, cementing his status as one of the sport's most marketable stars before his third NBA season has even tipped off.

The deal places Wembanyama in rare company. Signature Nike basketball shoes have historically been reserved for players who have proven themselves over years, sometimes decades, of sustained excellence. LeBron James, Kevin Durant and Giannis Antetokounmpo all waited. Wembanyama, who averaged 25.4 points, 10.7 rebounds and 3.6 blocks per game last season while leading San Antonio back toward playoff relevance, apparently convinced Nike the wait was unnecessary.

For the Spurs franchise, the announcement carries significance well beyond footwear. San Antonio has spent years rebuilding around Wembanyama as its cornerstone, and a Nike signature deal signals to the broader sports marketplace that the league's next generational face is already here. The specific design details and release timeline of the shoe have not yet been disclosed, but the basketball world will be watching every step.

story.headline: GRAF INKS THREE-YEAR DEAL WITH SHARKS AS OFFSEASON HEATS UP
story.deck: San Jose locks up productive forward while Pittsburgh extends Novak and league news swirls
story.body:
San Jose locked up one of its most reliable forwards Saturday, signing Collin Graf to a three-year contract worth $12.75 million. Graf, who posted 21 goals and 25 assists across 81 games last season, proved himself a consistent offensive contributor for a Sharks squad desperate to build around young talent. The deal averages $4.25 million per season and signals San Jose's intent to remain competitive as the franchise works through its rebuild.

In Pittsburgh, the Penguins moved to secure their own depth by signing dependable forward Tommy Novak to a three-year extension Friday. Novak has carved out a steady role as a reliable two-way presence, and the organization views him as an important piece of its transitional core. The contract adds stability to a Pittsburgh roster navigating uncertain waters in the post-Crosby era of roster reconstruction.

Elsewhere, the hockey world absorbed a pair of jarring international developments. Färjestad BK of the Swedish Elite League reversed course on a deal with defenseman Cal Foote after a wave of fan backlash forced the club's hand, leaving Foote's immediate future unresolved. The IIHF also confirmed Friday that Russia remains barred from four major tournaments in 2027, extending the federation's ongoing sanctions and further straining the relationship between Russian hockey and the broader international community.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: A flurry of signal-caller trades and signings is redefining the league's power structure.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a quarterback carousel unlike anything the league has seen in years, with franchises across both conferences gambling heavily on new faces under center as the calendar pushes toward summer training camps. The Cleveland Browns, long starved for stability at the position, are among the most aggressive movers, restructuring contracts and clearing cap space in pursuit of a proven starter who can finally end decades of organizational futility at the sport's most important position.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held in late April in Washington, D.C., produced its share of surprises, with several teams trading up aggressively to land prospects scouts had graded as potential franchise cornerstones. The Las Vegas Raiders used a pair of second-round picks to move into the top five, selecting a highly touted offensive tackle whose pass-blocking grades out of college drew comparisons to former All-Pro blindside protectors. Meanwhile, the New England Patriots, operating in their third full offseason since the Bill Belichick era ended, used multiple picks to address a defensive backfield that surrendered too many big plays throughout the 2025 campaign.

Training camps are scheduled to open in late July, but the storylines are already writing themselves. The Dallas Cowboys remain locked in tense negotiations with two veteran starters seeking long-term extensions, while the San Francisco 49ers are monitoring the recovery of a key skill-position player who underwent knee surgery in March. League observers expect the roster movement to continue well into June, as salary cap deadlines force general managers to make difficult decisions that will shape competitive windows for years to come.
